narrative.overview:
The day is a transit diagram printed on midnight enamel. The four food groups are four coloured lines running the full height of the day; each meal is a station where some lines stop and others pass through. Balance is read the way a rider reads a map, by which lines served a station, never as a score, ring, donut or calorie total. Everything else is signage: porcelain ink, condensed uppercase station names, square outlined buttons, thick porcelain rules under headers.

Density is wayfinding-calm rather than dashboard-busy: one diagram, a few station names, one coach question at a time. The energy comes from the saturated line inks against a deep ground and from the condensed display type, not from motion or decoration. The world is dark-first; a porcelain-ground light variant is unresolved and has not been built.

The system rejects the category default of white cards with macro donuts and progress rings.
keyCharacteristics: Four line inks are the only chromatic colours; everything else is enamel and porcelain.
Station dots, interchange rings and capsules are the only rounded forms; every control is square-cornered.
Barlow Condensed uppercase for anything you read like a sign; Barlow for anything you read like a sentence.
Structure is drawn with rules and outlines, not shadows.
Lines run straight and bend only at 45° or 90°.

rules.name: The One Line, One Group Rule
rules.body: Green, scarlet, amber and cobalt each belong to one food group. They never decorate, never mark success or failure, and never appear as backgrounds behind text.

rules.name: The Amber Signal Rule
rules.body: Starch amber doubles as the "you are here" and focus signal, so it always arrives with a shape (3px outline, interchange ring, 4px underline) and never as a colour change alone.

rules.name: The No Red Guilt Rule
rules.body: Protein scarlet is a line colour, not an error state. An absent line is drawn dashed and neutral, never in red.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Anything uppercase is Barlow Condensed with positive tracking (0.01–0.12em, wider as size drops). Barlow body text is never uppercased.

rules.name: The Self-Hosted Rule
rules.body: Fonts ship with the app as woff2 with `font-display: swap`; no font CDN, so the map renders identically offline.

rules.name: The 45/90 Rule
rules.body: Lines are straight. Where a diagram bends (brand mark, unlock map), it bends at 45° or 90° only. No curves, no organic paths.

rules.name: The Printed Map Rule
rules.body: Surfaces lie flat like a printed diagram. Separate planes with a rule (1–4px) or the raised enamel tone, never with blur.

rules.name: The Round Means Map Rule
rules.body: If it is round, it is part of the diagram (a stop, a ring, a station). UI chrome stays square.

dos: Do express balance only as which lines stopped at a station: dots on lines, line-bar cells, day-list segments.
Do pair every line colour with its name or a text summary ("Dairy passed through without a stop") so colour is never the only signal.
Do draw absent or pending states dashed and neutral (open station, missed stop, passed line).
Do keep controls square with 2px outlines and at least 48px targets (44px only for inline portion presets).
Do use starch amber for focus and "you are here", always with an outline, ring or underline shape.
Do put Barlow Condensed uppercase on names and actions and Barlow on sentences.
donts: Don't introduce rings, donuts, progress bars, scores or calorie totals to show balance.
Don't use a line ink for anything other than its food group, and don't use protein scarlet as an error or warning colour.
Don't round the corners of buttons, cards, chips, fields or sheets; roundness belongs to stops, rings and station capsules.
Don't add drop shadows or blur for depth; use the raised enamel plane or a rule.
Don't bend a line at any angle other than 45° or 90°.
Don't load fonts from a CDN.
**Don't** outline a control with the night rule (1.7:1). Unselected controls use the control edge (the raised control edge on the sheet and the dock); selected ones use porcelain.
